*   **Fine-tuning Iterations per New View:** 2,000 iterations total [S1].

The claim states that the fine-tuning iterations per new view are 2,000 iterations total. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the 'Implementation Details' section: 'For each newly added reference view... we continue the training of NeRF for 2000 iterations'. It further details that the first 100 iterations use only the new view and the remaining 1900 use all reference views, which sums to 2000. Thus, the evidence fully supports the claim.

*   **When to Use:** When only a single panorama is available and high-quality novel view synthesis is required [S1].

The claim states that the method is used 'When only a single panorama is available'. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly supports this in multiple places: Section 3.6 Algorithm states 'Input: A single panorama Irgb'; Algorithm 1 step 1 mentions 'Estimate a depth map Id of the given panorama Irgb'; and the Implementation Details section states 'To learn PERF, we first train NeRF with the single input panorama'. The claim also mentions 'high-quality novel view synthesis is required', which is the general goal of the PERF algorithm described in the text (generating novel views from a single input). Since all specific facts in the claim regarding the input condition (single panorama) are present and confirmed in the evidence, the verdict is supported.

*   **Limitations:** Relies on external models (Stable Diffusion, depth estimator) which may introduce artifacts if not properly aligned [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in the Implementation Details section that the method uses 'the pre-trained model from Stable-Diffusion-2 [61] as our inpainting model' and performs 'collaborative RGBD inpainting using a Stable Diffusion for RGB inpainting and a depth estimator for stitching'. This confirms the reliance on external models (Stable Diffusion and a depth estimator) as claimed.

*   **History:** The method builds on Instant-NGP [S1] and integrates recent advances in diffusion models for inpainting [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in the 'Implementation Details' section that 'We use Instant-NGP [40] for the representation of the NeRF model.' It also states that 'We use the pre-trained model from Stable-Diffusion-2 [61] as our inpainting model.' Stable Diffusion is a well-known diffusion model used for image generation and inpainting. Therefore, the claim that the method builds on Instant-NGP and integrates recent advances in diffusion models for inpainting is fully supported by the text.

It sets itself apart from standard single-view NeRF methods by integrating a collaborative RGBD inpainting step with a progressive erasing mechanism to handle the ambiguity of unseen geometry, building on the [NeRF Training Loop](970-nerf-training-loop.md) by dynamically expanding the reference view set [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source describes a method (PERF) that starts with a single-view NeRF (built on standard NeRF principles) and distinguishes itself by integrating 'collaborative RGBD inpainting' (Section 3.4) and a 'progressive inpainting-and-erasing scheme' (Section 3.5) to handle geometry conflicts and unseen regions. The source details the process of dynamically expanding the reference view set by sampling new views, inpainting them, erasing conflicted regions, and fine-tuning the NeRF, which aligns with the claim's description of handling ambiguity of unseen geometry and building on the NeRF training loop.
